before: Forwarding silence can reflect loss rather than misconduct, but censoring it also prevents missing observations from reversing earlier positive evidence. We examine this trade-off in a separately frozen 1,440-run Cooja factorial study and retain the earlier 750-, 180-, 240- and 600-run experiments. Twelve perturbed geometry blocks combine three retained checkpoints, two radio seeds per block, relay-identity permutations, both attacker positions, benign controls and two timing settings. Four matched arms vary missing-evidence penalties and proof generation while sharing ACK eligibility, expiry and positive-credit handling; an active-proof reference retains its legacy evidence semantics. With scheduled processing, enabling negative updates changes post-onset delivery by +21.170 percentage points (95% pointwise interval +14.410 to +27.834; Holm-adjusted p=0.005859). Enabling proof generation changes it by +1.017 percentage points (95% pointwise interval -0.826 to +2.906; Holm-adjusted p=0.668). Archive diagnostics find 7,023 risk-coordinate differences across 11,927 matched censored–frozen decisions without a relay-choice change; 1,010 of 4,800 offline risk interventions change actions. The O3 and LTO compiler profiles each miss 68 of 200 original signed-receipt deadlines. The contribution is auditable attribution of feedback and traffic interventions within a declared fixture family, rather than a new learning algorithm or a universal switching threshold. Public fixture keys, narrow geometry coverage and illustrative scheduled delays restrict security and deployment inference. Physical RF, measured energy and production device protections remain unvalidated.

after: The evaluated scope ends at radio simulation and compiled-MCU emulation. Physical RF/current acquisition, protected device keys, authenticated physical provisioning, firmware authenticity and reset-safe MCU persistence are outside that scope and have not been validated. The benchmark records virtual endpoint behavior, including deadline failures; it does not certify deployment readiness. Native Cooja scheduling assumptions provide neither a serial CPU model nor physical calibration.

before: Exploratory reconstruction explains the censored–frozen equality in the archived setting: recorded risk changes did not alter selected relays, although larger offline risk interventions could. Failure under the tested conditions therefore cannot be equated with complete actor insensitivity. Both O3 and LTO compiler profiles retain 68/200 signed-receipt deadline misses. The radio-current sensitivity in Section 5.12 also shows why lower transmit airtime alone cannot establish measured energy savings. The study supplies neither a universal switching threshold nor a production hardware validation. Physical RF, measured energy, protected device keys and reboot-persistent MCU state remain unvalidated.
